For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Updated SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

Below I identify where the Seller's draft departs from our playbook, with reasoning, then summarise recommendations. First, a framing caution.

## Framing: reject the "market / agreed / final" preamble

The preamble asserts these terms are "standard," "market," "settled at principal level by both deal teams," "reflect the agreed commercial bargain," and are "FINAL." **None of that binds us.** Per playbook sec 0.4/6.3, a position is not required-by-law, market-standard, agreed, final or pre-cleared merely because the counterparty's document says so. I have seen no confirmation through our own authority process that principals agreed anything here. Treat the whole preamble as negotiating rhetoric and the draft as the other side's opening position to be marked up. We should say so expressly so silence is not later read as acceptance.

---

## Material issues

### 1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1 (AUD 4,800,000 / 20%)
- Our starting position is **25% / AUD 6,000,000**. The 20% / AUD 4,800,000 figure is only a *conditional fallback* requiring **prior written authority from Amelia Frost** identifying the draft. No such authority has been given.
- Note the trap: the Seller's number happens to match our fallback. Per sec 6.3, a change is **not cleared merely because the number matches a fallback**. Do not let the coincidence drift into acceptance.
- **Push back to 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** Do not move to 20% without Frost's written sign-off.

### 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2
- Seller: de minimis **AUD 25,000**; basket **AUD 250,000**, and "only the excess above the basket is recoverable."
- Playbook: de minimis **AUD 5,000**; basket **AUD 50,000**; and crucially **first-dollar recovery** once the basket is exceeded — not an excess-only/deductible basket.
- Both numbers are 5x our positions, and the recovery mechanic is wrong. **Push back on all three.**

### 3. Time limits — Clause 12.3/13
- Seller: **18 months**. Playbook general period is **24 months**; 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's written approval (none given). **Push back to 24 months.**
- Separately, "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a **drafting override** that would sweep fundamental/title, tax, fraud etc. into the general regime. Reject — we require separate regimes (see below).

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties
- Seller wants capacity and title under the **same caps and time limits** as general warranties "for administrative simplicity." This directly collides with our requirement for a **separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** Reject outright.

### 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance apply to "all Claims" — 9.3/12.8/20.5
- Applying these to *all* Claims of any nature would capture **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**, and the fundamental/title/tax categories. Our playbook **carves fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable — and no one may waive this.** Insert an express, unwaivable fraud carve-out and keep categories separate.

### 6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]
- Seller relies on **whole-data-room deemed disclosure** (everything in the indexed data room as at 22 Sep 2026, DD-002–DD-012) plus **Accounts, statutory registers and public registers**. Our playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and **rejects whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure.** Reject [1.1] and [1.2]'s general sweep; require matters to be specifically and fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope.
- [1.4]'s "nothing admits… that any consent/payment/notice is legally required" is a reservation we can live with as neutral, but it should not be used to dilute specific disclosure or our substantive protections.

### 7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3
- This is a **blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion** extending to "any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (i.e., constructive/deemed knowledge). Playbook: **delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions.** Any qualifier must be tied to **actual knowledge of named buyer individuals**, and must **never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity**. Also reject the "discoverable" (constructive knowledge) limb entirely.

### 8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3/6.3 (and Disclosure §2)
- Seller offers **reasonable endeavours** and treats consent as **satisfied on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure §2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied** yet. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of revenue — plainly a **material customer**.
- Playbook: require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; **not consent-on-delivery**; **reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer**. Make effective, condition-satisfied consent a **Completion condition**.

### 9. Riverlark — Clause 2/7 (and Disclosure §3)
- Seller proposes **release following Completion**. Disclosure §3 confirms **not repaid, no discharge included**. Facility ~AUD 3.2m.
- Playbook: require **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases** at Completion. A **post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** (not given). Also confirm this is handled consistently with debt-free/cash-free — it should reduce what flows to Seller, not sit as a lingering buyer risk. Push for payout and release at Completion.

### 10. Employee bonuses — funds flow (and Disclosure §5)
- DD-005 bonuses **AUD 420,000** are "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised in the funds flow**; Disclosure §5 confirms they're omitted and is **silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs**.
- Playbook: the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them.** This is exactly the "silent exclusion" we must prevent. Require either explicit seller-funding or a funds-flow line item capturing the bonus **and** on-costs (payroll tax/super).

### 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1 (and Disclosure §4)
- Seller keeps the indemnity **narrowly limited to the SOW3 payment** and calls it "adequate." Disclosure §4 confirms **AUD 180,000 open, no independent bank verification, no receipt or confirmatory assignment**, and that clause 7.3 ties transfer of SOW3 Project Materials to **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**.
- Playbook: **broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure**; note the **AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way** — so don't concede it's owed, but don't accept Seller's "adequate" characterisation. We need protection covering loss of the Project Materials/IP if payment isn't cleared, not just the fee amount. Push to broaden.

### 12. Export/privacy incident — Clause 4.6/Schedule 6 (and Disclosure §6)
- Seller calls DD-006 "preliminary… not expected to be material." Disclosure §6: download link to an unintended external address, ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); **does not establish access, scope, or notification duty; no confirmed breach; no loss figure.**
- Playbook: **assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.** So we should neither accept Seller's dismissal nor assert a breach. Require: **preservation of logs, completion of the investigation, and ongoing updates**, plus an appropriate specific indemnity/conduct covenant for this identified matter so residual risk sits with Seller. Don't let it be waved away as immaterial.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals — AUD 330,000 (Disclosure §8)
- Seller labels the three renewals "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure §8 is **silent on whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.**
- Playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** So resist Seller's blanket "ordinary course" conclusion *and* resist treating it as Debt. Request the underlying terms (DD-008/DD-011) to assess termination/accrual before taking a position.

### 14. Title — (Seller "Title" item and Disclosure §10)
- Seller evidences 100% title **solely by the DD-012 share register**. Disclosure §10 admits this is **the source relied on** and that the **Buyer has not completed its own verification**.
- Playbook: **DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.** Require **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence** (e.g., independent confirmations, certificates, searches as to encumbrances and authority). Don't accept the internal register as sufficient.

### 15. Tax / IP — "settled under the general regime"
- Seller asserts tax and IP are "settled under the general regime." Playbook: **Tax/IP remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution; keep categories separate with no hidden general-regime override.** Reject the assertion that these are settled; they are open and must not be swept into the general cap/time regime by the clause 13 "all Claims" drafting.

### 16. Collateral points worth noting
- **Office lease (Disclosure §7)** and **Mossvale (§9)**: Seller says neither requires consent for the share sale. These appear less critical but we should verify the actual clauses rather than accept the characterisation — §7 flags a **notification obligation** we should ensure is complied with.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Our position / action |
|---|-------|----------------------|
| 1 | Reject preamble | State that "market/agreed/final" assertions are not accepted; nothing is cleared absent our own authority process. |
| 2 | Cap 12.1 | Push to **25% / AUD 6m**; do **not** accept 20% without Frost's written authority (fallback-match is not clearance). |
| 3 | Thresholds 12.2 | De minimis **AUD 5k**, basket **AUD 50k**, **first-dollar** recovery (reject excess-only). |
| 4 | Time limit 13 | **24 months** (18 needs Frost approval, not given); delete "all Claims" blanket limitation override. |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | Separate regime: **100% cap, ≥6 years**, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge. Reject "same as general." |
| 6 | Fraud carve-out | Insert **unwaivable** carve-out of fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. |
| 7 | Disclosure | Require **specific fair disclosure**; reject whole-data-room/public-register deemed disclosure. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge 8.3 | Delete blanket + "discoverable/constructive" exclusion; limit to actual knowledge of named persons; never cover title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnities. |
| 9 | Bluefen | **Effective consent + conditions satisfied before Completion** as a condition; reject reasonable-endeavours/consent-on-delivery for this material (~30%) customer. |
| 10 | Riverlark | **Payout + direct repayment from Completion funds + effective release at Completion**; post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval. |
| 11 | DD-005 bonuses | **AUD 420k + on-costs** as a funds-flow line item or seller-funded; no silent exclusion. |
| 12 | Ironquay | **Broaden** indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure; treat AUD 180k as unverified (neither conceded nor accepted as adequate). |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | Neutral stance: **preserve logs, investigate, ongoing updates**, specific conduct covenant/indemnity; assume no confirmed breach/harm/notification/number. |
| 14 | Sandbar | **Assess** the terms; reject blanket "ordinary course" and reject automatic Debt/price deduction. |
| 15 | Title | Require **independent** title/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is not independent proof. |
| 16 | Tax/IP | Treat as **OPEN**; no unlimited liability, no resolution, no general-regime override; keep categories separate. |

**Authority flags for the deal team:** three of the Seller's positions coincide with our *conditional fallbacks* (20% cap, 18-month period) or require escalation (post-completion Riverlark release). None of these may be conceded without **Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this specific draft**, which we do not have. I'd recommend confirming our opening mark-up at the *starting* positions and only engaging the fallbacks if and when Frost authorises.

Want me to turn this into a mark-up/issues list formatted for sending to Seller's counsel, or a shorter internal note for Amelia Frost to action the authority points?
=== END ADVICE ===
